direct_answer: Yes. Solvay discloses that it has a “transition plan for climate change mitigation” and a related “decarbonization roadmap”/roadmap reviewed by the Board of Directors [Source 1][Source 9]. However, Solvay explicitly states that its current targets/plan “are not compatible with the objective of limiting global warming to 1.5℃ in line with the Paris Agreement” [Source 1]. Instead, Solvay indicates its targets are aligned with a science-based scenario “well below 2℃” [Source 11] and notes it is “currently looking at how to accelerate the delivery of our projects” to align on a 1.5℃ target [Source 1]. As a transition plan exists, no timeline for adopting a plan is applicable/disclosed [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: Evidence shows Solvay has a transition plan/roadmap and provides key elements (targets, roadmap, governance/board review, and funding) [Source 1][Source 9][Source 2]. For ESRS E1-1.16(a), Solvay clearly addresses 1.5°C alignment by stating the plan/targets are not compatible with 1.5°C and that it is exploring acceleration to align [Source 1]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide the full ESRS E1-4 detail on science-based/1.5°C compatibility (e.g., specific methodology/framework for 1.5°C alignment, external assurance status for targets), beyond noting prior SBTi validation and “well below 2℃” alignment [Source 11][Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Explanation of how the transition plan’s GHG targets would become compatible with a 1.5°C pathway (beyond stating they are not compatible and that acceleration is being explored) [Source 1].

ESRS E1-4-type details on whether/how current targets are science-based and compatible with 1.5°C (framework/methodology, underlying climate and policy scenarios used for target-setting, and whether targets have been externally assured) are not provided in the retrieved passages [Source 11][Source 1].
A clear statement of a committed timeline/date to update targets/transition plan to achieve 1.5°C alignment is not disclosed in the retrieved passages [Source 1].
key_findings: Solvay has a climate change mitigation transition plan and decarbonization roadmap, designed to make its strategy/business model compatible with the transition to a sustainable economy [Source 1].
Targets disclosed: carbon neutral Scope 1 & 2 by 2050; by 2030 reduce Scope 1 & 2 by 30% and Scope 3 (focus 5 categories) by 20% vs 2021 baseline [Source 1][Source 11].
Solvay states these targets/plan are not compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C; it is exploring acceleration to align with 1.5°C [Source 1].
Solvay indicates its targets are aligned with a science-based scenario “well below 2℃” and references prior SBTi validation (March 2023) with an earlier baseline [Source 11][Source 1].

Governance and resourcing: the roadmap has been reviewed by the Board; decarbonization projects are integrated into financial planning and evaluated using an internal CO2 price of EUR 100/tCO2e; capex allocated and planned through 2030 and beyond [Source 9][Source 2].
